required_points.point: S.52 applies only if the specific immovable property is directly and specifically in question in the pending suit. A maintenance or money suit usually does not put a house in issue, so the memo must test this threshold against the facts.
required_points.evidence: The memo asserts that 'The right to maintenance and the ability to attach assets for recovery constitute a direct and specific right in question under the maintenance suit' but provides no factual analysis of whether the specific house was pleaded as subject-matter of the maintenance suit. The memo assumes s.52 applies without testing whether the house was 'directly and specifically in question' as required by the statute. It does not examine the maintenance suit pleadings to confirm the property was identified or claimed therein.

required_points.point: Where s.52 does apply, a transferee takes subject to the outcome of the suit even if bona fide and without notice.
required_points.evidence: The memo states: 'A transfer pendente lite is NOT void ab initio; the sale remains valid as between transferor and transferee. However, it is legally subservient to the decree in the pending suit and binds the transferee by the result.' This correctly articulates that subordination applies regardless of good faith or notice.

required_points.point: Memo must flag that Tabassum Shaheen and Muhammad Iqbal point different ways on s.41 versus lis pendens, and explain Iqbal's special facts (collusive consent decree, unimpleaded earlier purchaser).
required_points.evidence: The memo does not cite, discuss, or reference Tabassum Shaheen or Muhammad Iqbal at all. It cites only Mst. Rasool Bibi v. Ghulam Rasool (2007 YLR 2530) and Muhammad Yousuf v. Muhammad Alam Usmani (2007 YLR 2735), neither of which are the required authorities. The memo fails to address the divergent holdings or special facts of Iqbal regarding collusive consent decrees and unimpleaded purchasers.

required_points.point: S.41 requires a transfer for consideration, so a gift mutation cannot qualify. A mutation is only a record of title.
required_points.evidence: The memo correctly states: 'The brother received a gift (not even a purchase for value)' and 'A gift recipient (no consideration paid) has significantly weaker standing than even a purchaser for value.' It also notes 'Section 41 protects a purchaser for value without notice of any prior legal interest,' implicitly recognizing that a gift does not satisfy the consideration requirement.

required_points.point: S.53 TPA (transfer to defeat or delay creditors) is the more apt basis, with intent judged on the totality of circumstances.
required_points.evidence: The memo does not cite, discuss, or reference Section 53 TPA at all. It relies exclusively on Section 52 TPA (lis pendens) and does not present s.53 as an alternative or more apt basis for challenging the transfer on grounds of intent to defeat or delay creditors.

required_points.point: S.47 CPC covers parties and their representatives. O.XXI r.58 is the specific route for objections to attachment, and the order is open to a separate suit (lawyer to confirm rule numbers).
required_points.evidence: The memo correctly states: 'Section 47 CPC applies to questions arising between the parties to the suit as to the discharge or satisfaction of the decree. The executing court CAN decide questions between the judgment-creditor (your client) and the judgment-debtor (ex-husband) under Section 47. For third-party title objections, the proper procedure is Order XXI Rule 58 CPC, not Section 47.' However, the memo does not explicitly flag that an Order XXI Rule 58 order is not final and that a separate suit may follow.

required_points.point: Courts may allow amendment at any stage but must exercise the discretion with caution.
required_points.evidence: Order VI, Rule 17, CPC confers discretionary authority on courts to permit amendments to pleadings... The discretionary language of Order VI, Rule 17, however, does not mean amendments can be allowed indefinitely or in disregard of principles of natural justice and procedural fairness.

required_points.point: An amendment is refused if it alters the nature of the suit, withdraws admissions, is mala fide, prejudices the other side, or tries to overcome evidentiary contradictions.
required_points.evidence: amendments are subject to: (1) No prejudice to the opposite party (or justified grounds notwithstanding prejudice), and (2) Reasonable cause or justification for any delay in seeking the amendment... The Court held (per headnote): Belated amendments introducing new factual assertions, without credible justification and likely to prejudice the opposing party, cannot be permitted under Order VI, Rule 17, CPC.

required_points.point: A belated amendment adding a new factual assertion needs heightened scrutiny.
required_points.evidence: The location of an alleged oral agreement to sell is likely to be classified as a central factual assertion rather than a peripheral detail... Adding a specific location (e.g., in the drawing room of the same house) after ten years is not merely clarifying an already-pleaded general fact; it is introducing new particularity to a disputed foundational claim.

required_points.point: A ten-year delay without a credible explanation weighs heavily against the applicant.
required_points.evidence: A ten-year delay in seeking an amendment is inordinate by any measure... In the context of a ten-year delay, the burden on the applicant to justify the omission is very high... Generic explanations (we overlooked it, we thought it was not important, counsel failed to include it) will likely be insufficient.

required_points.point: Correcting a typographical error is treated differently from adding a key disputed fact.
required_points.evidence: Distinguish between a mere 'clarification' of an already-pleaded fact and an entirely 'new assertion.' If your original plaint stated 'an oral agreement was made at the respondent's residence,' you might argue that adding 'in the drawing room' is mere clarification. If the plaint was silent on location, this argument will fail.

Saying delay alone is always conclusive.
Saying the court cannot allow amendment after evidence has started.

required_points.point: A general attorney needs the principal's prior special permission to transfer property to himself or close relatives.
required_points.evidence: Allah Bakhsh v. Muhammad Riaz (2025 PLD 63) states: 'It is established law that holder of a general power of attorney must obtain special permission from the principal when alienating the principal's property, either in their own favor or in the name of their relatives.' Also Phulmajeeran Begum (2008 YLR 2841): 'Agent in such like cases possesses dominant influence and thus, could not be permitted to enter into any agreement to sell with a person of his own choice without there being an expressed permission by the Principal.'

required_points.point: If no such permission is shown, the sale's legality is highly doubtful.
required_points.evidence: Allah Bakhsh v. Muhammad Riaz (2025 PLD 63) explicitly states: 'In the absence of such permission, the legality and propriety of the alleged sale deed in favor of these individuals is highly doubtful.'

required_points.point: A deed running over several pages needs signatures on each page or proof connecting the pages.
required_points.evidence: This requirement is not addressed anywhere in the memorandum. The memo discusses authorization, consent, and burden of proof but does not address the technical requirement for signatures on each page of a multi-page deed.

required_points.point: Courts deciding objections to an award should avoid framing issues and recording evidence unless absolutely necessary.
required_points.evidence: The memo states: 'The objections procedure is summary in nature, requiring the Court to determine whether the arbitrator exceeded jurisdiction, committed misconduct or breach of natural justice, or committed patent procedural error—it does not require a full trial on the merits or recording of oral and documentary evidence on factual disputes.' The memo also emphasizes that 'framing of issues and calling for evidence' is 'fundamentally incorrect and constitutionally impermissible.'

required_points.point: An order framing issues must show why it is necessary, and the issues must be specific.
required_points.evidence: The memo does not address the requirement that an order framing issues must demonstrate necessity or that issues must be specific. The memo criticizes the framing of 'generalized issues of fact' but does not articulate the standard that specific, necessary issues might be permissible.

required_points.point: Courts are not appellate forums over awards. Interference is limited to jurisdictional error, proven misconduct or a patent legal error on the face of the record.
required_points.evidence: The memo states: 'The Court's jurisdiction is strictly limited to considering statutory objections under Sections 30 and 33 on narrow grounds of procedural defect, jurisdictional overreach, or breach of natural justice—not on the merits or facts of the underlying contract dispute.' It also notes: 'Recording of evidence and conducting a trial effectively converts the Court into an appellate or fact-finding forum, which would be contrary to the statutory scheme.'

required_points.point: The memo must confirm which arbitration statute governs the dispute.
required_points.evidence: The memo identifies the governing statute as the 'Arbitration Act, 1940' and references 'Sections 30 & 33 of the Arbitration Act, 1940' and 'Section 12-A of the Arbitration Act 1940' throughout.

forbidden_claims.forbidden_claim: Saying courts may re-appraise the evidence like a first appellate court.
Saying issues can never be framed (the Court said avoid unless necessary).
forbidden_claims.quote: The memo states: 'The Arbitration Act 1940 does not empower the civil court to frame issues of fact, call for evidence, or conduct a trial on objections to an award.' This is an absolute prohibition rather than a qualified 'avoid unless necessary' standard. The memo does not acknowledge that issues may be framed when necessary.
